subject: Order Form: payment rail design, invoice entity split & VAT residency
messages:
From: Alice Moreno <alice.moreno@gridline.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: tom.li@gridline.com
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form questions — invoice remit and VAT residency

Hi Olga / Ben,

Thanks for the demo last week — excited to move forward. Procurement has a couple of practical asks related to the Order Form and PO so we can get finance lined up quickly:

- Gridline will be onboarding EU-based clusters (Ireland + Germany). Our tax team needs clarity on which legal entity will receive invoices and bear VAT liability. The PO we attached is currently issued to Gridline Ltd (UK).
- We'd like to propose two possible payment rails:
  1) Single-invoice model: Redwood invoices Gridline Ltd for all usage (Gridline will self-account for VAT via reverse charge).
  2) Multi-entity model: Redwood issues invoices to Gridline Ireland (for EU usage) and Gridline Ltd for US/ROW — each entity receives separate invoices and local VAT is applied.
- Activation fee: can this be prorated across entities for a split-billing scenario?
- Net terms: standard Gridline request is Net45 — please confirm Redwood's flexibility.

Could you confirm which option is more feasible operationally and whether you need any tax residency evidence from our side? We're happy to loop in our tax ops. We attached the PO and a tentative billing matrix for illustration.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Moreno
Head of Procurement, Gridline Health
Attachments: Gridline_PO_202608.pdf (application/pdf), payment_matrix.csv (text/csv)
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Moreno <alice.moreno@gridline.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 12:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form questions — invoice remit and VAT residency

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear note and the PO.

On Sat, Aug 29, 2026 at 09:12 AM Alice Moreno <alice.moreno@gridline.com> wrote:
> Hi Olga / Ben,
> 
> Thanks for the demo last week — excited to move forward. Procurement has a couple of practical asks related to the Order Form and PO so we can get finance lined up quickly:
> ...

Quick summary from our side and what we need to confirm:

- Feasibility: Both payment rails are operationally doable but have trade-offs.
  * Single-invoice model (Option 1): simpler ops — one invoice, one remit. Customer self-manages VAT (reverse charge). Requires a contractual acknowledgement in the Order Form and an Export Control / Tax residency clause in the SOW so finance knows to accept a single legal entity invoice for multiple regions.
  * Multi-entity model (Option 2): more work on invoicing and bookkeeping but cleaner for VAT — we apply local VAT where required and bill the appropriate entity. This requires us to split the Order Form invoicing appendix and add explicit entity mapping for each SKU/region.

- Activation fee proration: we can prorate the activation fee across entities if Gridline provides the entity allocation percentages. We will reflect the split in the invoice lines and in the Order Form annex.

- Net terms: Redwood typically offers Net30 on self-serve/hosted contracts and can extend to Net45 for enterprise deals with approved credit. Ben / Kimberly — can you confirm credit approval for Net45 on this deal?

Next steps I propose:
1) Ben / Kimberly to confirm commercial posture (Net45 / activation fee acceptance).
2) I'll attach a redline of the Order Form that covers both Option 1 and Option 2 language so legal has both paths to choose from.
3) If Gridline prefers Option 2, please provide a final entity allocation spreadsheet (percentages) and VAT registration docs for the receiving entities.

Attaching: OrderForm_Redline_v1.docx (contains two alternative invoicing annexes + tracked changes).

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Contracts Manager | Redwood Inference
Attachments: OrderForm_Redline_v1.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form questions — invoice remit and VAT residency

Olga / Kim — quick commercial note: agree with Olga's assessment. From a sales/CS standpoint we prefer Option 2 for Gridline because:
- Their tax team wants explicit VAT on EU invoices and less manual reconciliation on their side.
- Option 2 reduces billing disputes at renewal and is cleaner for our revenue ops.

Commercial asks:
- Accept Net45 for this enterprise PO (we'll mark deal for credit review).
- Prorate activation fee proportionally per the entity allocation Gridline will provide (10% of activation fee to Ireland, 90% to UK is fine as an example).

Kim — can you push the credit approval and confirm if Finance can accept split invoices into multiple legal entities under this MSA? If legal needs any MSA edits beyond the invoicing annex, flag them here and Olga will incorporate.

- Ben
Sales Director, Redwood Inference
From: Tom Li <tom.li@gridline.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Moreno <alice.moreno@gridline.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form questions — invoice remit and VAT residency

Ben / Olga — thanks for the options and the redline. Gridline Finance prefers Option 2 (multi-entity split). Our requests to make it production-ready: 

- We'll send a short entity allocation CSV (attached) with percent splits per line item. Please invoice Gridline Ireland (VAT ID: IE1234567V) for EU usage and Gridline Ltd (VAT ID: GB9876543) for non-EU usage.
- Activation fee: please prorate per provided allocation on the invoice line.
- Net45 is acceptable; we will return a signed PO once the Order Form annex contains the multi-entity invoicing appendix you proposed.
- Please include a single combined summary invoice for our internal apportionment reporting (separate legal invoices are the source of truth).

We attached the entity allocation CSV. If you can provide a final redline that includes the entity mapping clause and a sample invoice layout, we'll sign and route for payment.

Thanks,
Tom Li
Finance Manager, Gridline Health
Attachments: payment_matrix.csv (text/csv)
